title: Python for ML engineering
summary: The Python an ML engineer actually needs: NumPy's memory model, vectorization and broadcasting, numerical hygiene, SQL and DataFrames for telemetry, ML code written as software, and the testing and tooling that keep it correct.
objectives: Predict NumPy's behaviour (views vs copies, dtypes, broadcasting) before running code
Replace Python loops with vectorized, broadcasting array code and measure the speedup
Write numerically stable code (log-sum-exp, stable softmax) and explain floating-point traps
Query and resample sensor telemetry with SQL (DuckDB) and DataFrames (Polars, pandas), choosing the right tool
Structure ML code with types, dataclasses and the fit/predict contract, with seeded randomness
Test ML code with pytest, numerical tolerances and property-based tests, in a uv project

build.title: Telemetry toolkit
build.summary: A typed, tested Python package that loads simulator telemetry from Parquet, cleans gaps, stuck sensors and unit mix-ups, computes interval PUE, and exposes a small CLI.
